key_insight: Quantum classifiers can achieve competitive overall performance while retaining subgroup disparities, and smaller fairness gaps can mask performance losses.
clinical_relevance: Medical imaging AI evaluation should assess subgroup fairness alongside overall discrimination to avoid mistaking degraded performance for meaningful equity gains.
method: Audited SVM, MLP, QSVM and QCNN using ResNet-18 embeddings.
Compared baseline models with Equalized Odds regularisation, Gradient Reversal Learning and both combined.
Checked mitigation against a pre-specified non-inferiority margin; used PanDerm and EVA-X as external references.
evidence_signal: Across DDI skin-type groups and CheXpert-derived age groups, QSVM with combined mitigation performed best on DDI, while QCNN with Gradient Reversal Learning led aggregate performance on CheXpert but increased disparity.
watch_item: All quantum models ran in classical simulation; these findings do not establish quantum advantage or clinical readiness.
paper_title: Responsible Quantum Machine Learning for Medical Imaging: A Fairness Audit Across Sensitive Subgroups
